bib.title: DeepSeekMath: Pushing the Limits of Mathematical Reasoning in Open Language Models

question: Can a 7B open model reach near-GPT-4 competition math accuracy via web-mined math pre-training plus a memory-light RL algorithm (GRPO)?
hypothesis: Code training and high-quality web math data improve math reasoning, and critic-free group-relative RL improves an instruction-tuned model.
contributions: DeepSeekMath Corpus: 120B math tokens from Common Crawl via iterative fastText selection
DeepSeekMath-Base/Instruct/RL 7B; RL model exceeds 50% on MATH among open models
Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), PPO variant without a critic
Unified paradigm (data source, reward function, gradient coefficient) covering SFT, RFT, DPO, PPO, GRPO
Findings: code training helps math, arXiv does not

method.summary: Continue pretraining DeepSeek-Coder-Base-v1.5 7B on 500B tokens (56% DeepSeekMath Corpus), SFT on 776K math instructions, then RL with GRPO, which samples G outputs per question and uses group-normalised rewards as advantages instead of a value model, with KL added to the loss.
method.task: math pretraining, SFT and RL for mathematical reasoning

datasets.name: DeepSeekMath Corpus
datasets.size: 120B tokens, 35.5M web pages (89B-token version from iteration 2 used in Sec 5.1 ablations)
datasets.source: Common Crawl, 40B deduplicated HTML pages; seed OpenWebMath; fastText with 500K positive and 500K negative, dim 256, lr 0.1, wordNgrams 3, minCount 3, 3 epochs
datasets.preprocessing: URL dedup and near-dedup; 10-gram exact match decontamination against GSM8K, MATH, CMATH, AGIEval; exact match for benchmark texts of 3 to 9 grams

datasets.name: Math SFT data
datasets.source: GSM8K/MATH annotated with tool-integrated solutions, MathInstruct subset, Lila-OOD train, Chinese K-12 problems over 76 sub-topics
datasets.preprocessing: CoT, PoT and tool-integrated formats; examples randomly concatenated to 4K tokens

datasets.name: RL questions
datasets.source: CoT-format GSM8K and MATH related questions from the SFT data

datasets.name: GSM8K, MATH, OCW, SAT, MMLU-STEM, MGSM-zh, CMATH, Gaokao-MathCloze, Gaokao-MathQA, miniF2F, MMLU, BBH, HumanEval, MBPP

other.use: corpus and code/arXiv ablations; also 1.3B Instruct for Fig 5

other.data: constructed following Wang et al. 2023b (Math-Shepherd); replay with 10% historical data in iterative RL

training.objective: Pretraining: next token. SFT: next token on 776K. RL: GRPO objective (Eq 3) with clipped ratio, group-normalised advantage A_i = (r_i - mean(r))/std(r), KL to reference via unbiased estimator added to the loss
training.lr: Pretraining 1.3B: 5.3e-4 peak; Base 7B: 4.2e-4 peak; SFT: 5e-5 constant; reward model: 2e-5; RL policy: 1e-6
training.lr_schedule: multi-step: peak after 2,000 warmup steps, 31.6% of peak after 80% of training, 10.0% after 90%
training.batch_size: 1.3B pretraining: 4M tokens; 7B Base: 10M tokens; SFT: 256; RL: 1024
training.steps: SFT: 500 steps; RL steps not stated (Fig 5 axis to ~8000 for 1.3B, Fig 6 to ~5300)
training.tokens: 1.3B ablations: 150B per corpus (code ablation: 400B code/general then 150B math); Base 7B: 500B (56% DeepSeekMath Corpus, 4% AlgebraicStack, 10% arXiv, 20% GitHub code, 10% Common Crawl natural language EN/ZH); arXiv ablation: 7B 40B tokens
training.regularisation: KL coefficient beta 0.04 to reference; clip epsilon not stated

other.rl_updates_per_exploration: single update (mu=1), so old policy equals current
other.iterative_rl: reference model reset to current policy each iteration; reward model retrained with 10% replay; two iterations in Fig 6

inference.decoding: temperature 0.7 for Maj@K/Pass@K (Fig 7); nucleus sampling in RL (naive)
inference.samples: RL: 64 outputs per question; Table 5 grey: majority vote over 32 candidates; Fig 7: K from 1 to 64; abstract: 64 samples self-consistency
inference.prompting: few-shot CoT (math, MMLU, BBH), few-shot program-of-thought with Python (math and sympy), few-shot Isabelle proof sketches + Sledgehammer for miniF2F; HumanEval zero-shot, MBPP few-shot; shot counts not stated

metrics.name: Maj@K
metrics.definition: majority vote over K sampled answers

metrics.name: Pass@K
metrics.definition: at least one of K samples correct

eval.protocol: Single runs; no seeds or significance tests stated; benchmark contamination filtered by n-gram match.

evidence.quote: The policy model only has a single update following each exploration stage.

results.claim: GRPO RL lifts DeepSeekMath-Instruct 7B on MATH from 46.8% to 51.7% (CoT, no tools, Top1), using only GSM8K/MATH-related CoT SFT questions.
results.setup: DeepSeekMath-Instruct 7B to RL, chain-of-thought, Top1, no tools; RL data ~144K GSM8K/MATH-related CoT questions
DeepSeekMath-Instruct 7B to RL, chain-of-thought, Top1, no tools

results.claim: Out-of-domain gain: CMATH improves from 84.6% to 88.8% after RL on English GSM8K/MATH-style data only.
DeepSeekMath-RL 7B with tool-integrated reasoning reaches 58.8% on MATH (Instruct 57.4%).
results.setup: Tool-integrated reasoning, Top1 (Table 5 grey scores are majority vote of 32)
results.table: Table 5, Tool-Integrated Reasoning, row DeepSeekMath-RL 7B, column MATH

results.table: Table 5, CoT, row DeepSeekMath-RL 7B, column MGSM-zh

results.claim: Self-consistency over 64 samples from DeepSeekMath 7B gives 60.9% on MATH.
results.quote: Self-consistency over 64 samples from DeepSeekMath 7B achieves 60.9% on MATH.

results.claim: RL improves Maj@K but not Pass@K: RL sharpens the output distribution rather than adding fundamental capability.
results.setup: Instruct vs RL 7B, GSM8K and MATH, temperature 0.7, K in 1..64 (read from Fig 7)
results.quote: RL enhances Maj@K’s performance but not Pass@K.

results.setup: Common Crawl, 40B deduplicated HTML pages, fastText iterative selection
results.quote: we end up with 35.5M mathematical web pages, totaling 120B tokens

results.claim: 1.3B model trained 150B tokens on DeepSeekMath Corpus scores GSM8K 23.8%, MATH 13.6% vs OpenWebMath 11.5%/8.9% and Proof-Pile-2 14.3%/11.2%.

results.table: Table 1, row DeepSeekMath Corpus, column GSM8K

results.claim: RL hyperparameters: policy lr 1e-6, KL coefficient 0.04, 64 outputs per question, max length 1024, batch size 1024.
results.quote: For each question, we sample 64 outputs.

results.claim: Math training raises MMLU from 49.1% to 54.9% and BBH from 55.2% to 59.5%; HumanEval 43.2% to 40.9%.

limits: Authors: geometry and theorem-proof weaker than closed models; fails on triangles and ellipses, suggesting data selection bias.
Authors: few-shot performance does not improve over zero-shot, unlike GPT-4.
Authors: arXiv conclusion not tested on other tasks, in combination with other data, or at larger scale.
RL gains appear to come from boosting correct answers into top-K (Maj@K up, Pass@K flat); RL used only SFT questions and naive nucleus sampling.
Code-math one-stage mixture hurts no-tool math at 1.3B; authors conjecture limited capacity.
No hardware, compute, seeds, precision or clip epsilon reported; RL step count not stated; reward model details deferred to Wang et al. 2023b.
DPO and RFT are only analysed in the unified framework; Fig 5 compares RFT, Online RFT, GRPO (no DPO run is reported).

terms.definition: Group Relative Policy Optimization: samples a group of outputs per question and uses the average group reward as the baseline, removing the value model
gradient of a training method = E over Data Source of (1/|o|) sum_t GradientCoefficient(q,o,t,reward) * grad log pi(o_t|q,o_<t); components: data source, reward function, algorithm

lineage.note: GRPO is a PPO variant without value model
Analysed in the unified paradigm (Appendix A.1.4); gradient coefficient Eq 14
